title: Reinstate a suspended organization
description:
**Phase 2 of 7.**

- **Blocked by:** 41d08d
- **Runs in parallel with:** anything
- **Unblocks:** nothing

---
**Found reviewing #132.** Separating approval from reinstatement was correct. It is currently half-done.

`enable` refuses any organization that is not `PENDING`, `suspend` refuses any that is not `ENABLED`, and no operation moves an organization out of `SUSPENDED`. It is a terminal state reachable in one command and escapable in none.

**Do:** a `reinstate` operation on the kernel and a `reinstate` subcommand on the members CLI, allowed only from `SUSPENDED`, carrying the same confirmation and summary that `enable` does.

Keep it a separate name rather than relaxing `enable`. The whole point is that approving a new organization and reversing a deliberate intervention appear in the record as different acts by different people at different moments. A reinstatement should be as legible after the fact as the suspension was.

**Done when:** an organization can go pending to enabled to suspended to enabled again, every transition is refused from the wrong state, and the scenarios cover the round trip.
